question.:question/problem:
The birth rate of crocodiles in a river is modeled by $B(t) = 6 \cdot e^{0.25t}$ crocodiles per year, while the rate of death is modeled by $D(t) = 4 \cdot e^{0.25t}$ crocodiles per year, where $t$ represents the number of years since the year $2000$.

What was the rate of change of the crocodile population in $2012$? Round your answer to the nearest integer.

> A scientific calculator is required to answer this question.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The rate of change of the crocodile population is the birth rate minus the death rate.

$$
B(t)-D(t).
$$

Since $2012$ is $12$ years after $2000$, substitute $t=12$.

$$
\begin{aligned}B(12)-D(12) & =6\cdot e^{0.25(12)}-4\cdot e^{0.25(12)} \\  & =2\cdot e^{3} \\  & \approx 40.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the rate of change is $40$ crocodiles per year.

$$
\begin{aligned}O(t)-C(t) & =100(28){e}^{-0.1(28)}-(50+10sin⁡(\frac{2\pi }{7}(28))) \\  & =100(28){e}^{-2.8}-50-10sin⁡(8 \pi) \\  & =100(28){e}^{-2.8}-50 \\  & ≈120.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the rate of change in the number of cars in construction after $28$ days is $120$ cars per day.

$$
\begin{aligned}O(t)-C(t) & =50(40){e}^{-0.2(40)}-(60+20sin⁡(\frac{2\pi }{10}(40))) \\  & =50(40){e}^{-8}-60-20sin⁡(8 \pi) \\  & =50(40){e}^{-8}-60 \\  & ≈-59.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the rate of change in the number of cars in construction after $40$ days is $-59$ cars per day.
